(c) 38 is fully free with four off-edges; moving it onto col 17 under 12 converts 38-12 diag->V (trading the 38-23 diag away, HV first). (d) 33 is col-locked at 7 and free in the row: r14->r16 puts it on 16's locked row 16 (16-33 H) and keeps the whole col-7 spine 35-45-33-15 vertical; 43 steps to (3,13) as a staging move so next round it can reach row 16 for 33-43 H without a single long jump. (f) In the SW tail, 28 is row-locked at 20 and 51 is col-locked at 6, so 28 slides west onto col 6 (28-51 V); 50 is col-locked at 6 and slides down onto 49's locked row 25 (50-49 H). (g) 34 is row-locked at 14 and 55 col-locked at 20, so 34 slides east onto col 20 (34-55 V). Every slide was checked against the bearing order of its interchange neighbours (44/40/36/58/23, 33/16, 39/25, 51/27, 49) so the 360deg winding is preserved.

(b) 42 is degree-1; 39 is now doubly locked at (10,17), so instead of leaving 39-42 at 45deg I pull 42 onto 39's column (c8->c10) and upgrade the 45deg to a true V — HV is the primary key, so trading one 45deg for one H/V is always right. (c) 38 is now col-locked at 17 by the V it gained last round but still free in the row; of its three remaining off-edges only 18(11,8) offers an H/V, so r12->r8 closes 38-18 as H. Checked that the lengthened col-17 vertical (rows 8-13) swallows no vertex and that the new row-8 horizontal crosses no vertical in the empty cols 12/14/16. (d) 4-47 cannot reach H/V at all (47 is col-locked at 1 and must stay south of 8(1,3), 4 is row-locked at 6), so it is a pure 45deg target: sliding 4 two east along its own locked row and 47 two north inside its allowed range makes dx=dy=4. Every move re-checked against the bearing order at 33, 39, 38, 18, 23 and 12.

Round 3 — the H/V ceiling is reached: of the seven still-unaligned segments (45-36, 36-23, 13-38, 38-23, 23-20, 16-15, 2-18) every endpoint except 2 and 3 is now locked on BOTH axes by a segment it must not break, and 2-18 cannot go V because col 11 already holds 37(11,7) between them (the vertex would be swallowed) while 18 itself is col-locked. So this round works the secondary key instead: 2 is row-locked at 5 but free in the column, and 3 is row-locked at 1 but free in the column, so I move the pair together — 2 west to col 14 makes 2-18 dx=-3/dy=+3 (45deg), and 3 east to col 18 keeps 2-3 at dx=4/dy=-4 (45deg) instead of losing it. Moving only 2 would have been a wash (one 45deg gained, one lost); moving both is a net +1 on HVD with HV untouched. Verified the lengthened row-1 horizontal 1-3 crosses no vertical (it passes just south of 21(18,2), outside the col-18 21-6 span) and that the 2-3 diagonal clears 5(17,4) and 21(18,2).

Last round the pair was proposed together and 3 was bounced (the axial fallback could not split it either), so this time it is a single-vertex batch against the already-settled position of 2 — if the winding at 2 was the blocker it should now evaluate against 2's final bearing rather than its pre-move one.

Round 5 (final) — 3 was bounced twice at (18,1), so the 2/3 pair can only ever hold ONE of its two 45deg edges: with 2 at (14,5) it is 2-18, with 2 at (17,5) it is 2-3. The two are score-identical (HV 62, HVD 67 either way), so I pick the variant that is better for what comes next: 2 back at (17,5) vacates col 14, which restores it to the empty-column set (8, 12, 14, 16) that the network loop can compact away, and it also shortens the row-5 horizontal 2-13 from 4 cells to 1. HV is at its ceiling: all seven remaining unaligned segments (45-36, 36-23, 13-38, 38-23, 23-20, 16-15, 2-3) have both endpoints locked on both axes — every one of them is an interchange already carrying an H and a V it must not break — so no further short move can add an H/V without destroying one.
